jaap.theme: Remembering the One who cannot be contained in labels
jaap.simpleEn: Jaap Sahib offers many names and descriptions of the One while reminding us that the Divine cannot be limited to a body, caste, colour, appearance or human category. Its repeated salutations turn language itself into attentive praise.
jaap.simplePa: ਜਾਪੁ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਗੁਣ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਰੱਬ ਨੂੰ ਰੂਪ, ਰੰਗ, ਜਾਤ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਇਕ ਨਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ। ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਇਕਾਗਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap.deeperEn: The opening refuses to reduce the Divine to a picture or social identity. Later chhands praise the One with many attributes, rhythmic names and poetic contrasts. The apparent paradox matters: we name what cannot be completely named. The names are ways of turning attention toward the One, not a list of independent gods.
words: A salutation: I bow to You
jaap.caution: Jaap uses diverse Braj, Sanskritic and Persian-influenced word forms. Specific etymologies, metre names, pronunciation and 67 source-variant groups remain editorially unapproved.
jaap.reflection: If the Divine is not confined to human labels, what happens when I judge people only by appearance or status?
jaap.question: Why does Jaap Sahib use many names while saying that no label can fully define the One?

savaiye.theme: Love and sincerity matter more than display
savaiye.simpleEn: These ten Savaiye question whether rituals, wealth, political power, outward spiritual appearances or military strength can bring us near the Divine without sincere love and devotion. The message is not to abandon ethical action; it is to avoid mistaking display for inner transformation.
savaiye.simplePa: ਦਸ ਸਵੱਯੇ ਪੁੱਛਦੇ ਹਨ: ਜੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿਚ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਤੇ ਸੱਚੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਨਹੀਂ, ਤਾਂ ਦਿਖਾਵਾ, ਧਨ, ਤਾਕਤ ਜਾਂ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਰਸਮਾਂ ਕਿੰਨਾ ਕੰਮ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ? ਇਹ ਚੰਗੇ ਕਰਮ ਛੱਡਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਦਿਲ ਦੀ ਸਚਾਈ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਹੈ।
savaiye.deeperEn: The poems build their argument with striking examples: ascetics, kings, armies and worship practices. Each can impress observers, but the text continually asks what gives a life spiritual weight. Savaiya 9 states its emphasis on love especially clearly. When studying, separate the poem’s critique of hollow practice from a broad claim that all religious disciplines or communities are worthless.
words: A religious practitioner; exact historical usage needs review
savaiye.caution: This is the morning group beginning Sravag Sudh, not the evening Pae Gahe Savaiya in Rehras. Unresolved digital spelling differences require comparison with a named source edition.
savaiye.reflection: Where can a small sincere act express more love than an impressive outward display?
savaiye.question: What distinction do these Savaiye make between religious appearance and loving devotion?

chaupai.theme: A prayer for protection and steadfastness
chaupai.simpleEn: Benti Chaupai speaks in the voice of someone asking the Divine for protection, courage, guidance and support. It also asks that the mind remain turned toward the One. Its forceful language about enemies must be read with literary and historical care rather than applied casually to other people.
chaupai.simplePa: ਬੇਨਤੀ ਚੌਪਈ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਖਿਆ, ਹੌਸਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਹਾਰਾ ਮੰਗਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮਨ ਰੱਬ ਦੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਰਹੇ—ਇਹ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਵੀ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਤਿੱਖੀ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਸਮਝਣ ਲਈ ਸੰਦਰਭ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ।
chaupai.deeperEn: The opening verses seek refuge and request that fear not overwhelm the speaker. The prayer repeatedly expresses dependence upon the Divine while using the heightened imagery of a martial literary world. A responsible learning lesson distinguishes the actual wording from a proposed modern psychological application; neither the text nor the app authorizes aggression against a person.
words: Feet; often a metaphor for humble refuge
chaupai.caution: The current reader uses an explicitly named expanded 29-pauri website candidate. The shorter 25-pauri evening Rehras excerpt and other accepted traditions require separate source and community review.
chaupai.reflection: What does it mean to ask for courage while also accepting responsibility for our actions?
chaupai.question: Which phrases ask for protection, and which ask for closeness to the Divine?

anand.theme: The steadier joy of understanding and living the Guru’s wisdom
anand.simpleEn: Anand Sahib explores joy that goes deeper than brief pleasures. Guru Amar Das describes a life transformed through the Guru’s wisdom, remembrance of the One, inner steadiness and freedom from consuming attachment.
anand.simplePa: ਅਨੰਦੁ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਥੋੜ੍ਹੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਡੂੰਘੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ, ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਮਨ ਦੀ ਸਹਜ ਅਵਸਥਾ ਨਾਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਵਿਚ ਟਿਕਾਊ ਖਿੜਾਉ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
anand.deeperEn: The composition begins with an expression of discovery: bliss has arisen because the Guru has been found. The following pauris address the mind, the True One, Naam and inner transformation. Its forty-pauri journey is not a promise that every follower will always feel happy or never experience pain; the concept of anand is richer than a temporary pleasant mood.
anand.caution: The digital original contains an unresolved private-use Unicode glyph in Pauri 24, withheld in our reader. The full 40-pauri morning composition must not be silently replaced by the first five plus last pauri used within Rehras.
anand.reflection: Can inner steadiness coexist with a difficult day?
anand.question: How does the opening of Anand Sahib connect joy to the Guru rather than possessions?

rehras.theme: Evening remembrance, humility, gratitude and renewed courage
rehras.simpleEn: Rehras gathers hymns from Sri Guru Granth Sahib and passages from Dasam Bani into an evening prayer. It remembers the vastness of the One, our dependence on grace, courage through fear, and the opportunity to live purposefully.
rehras.simplePa: ਰਹਿਰਾਸਿ ਸ਼ਾਮ ਵੇਲੇ ਰੱਬ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ, ਸ਼ੁਕਰਾਨੇ ਅਤੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਵਿਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਅਤੇ ਦਸਮ ਬਾਣੀ ਦੇ ਭਾਗ ਇੱਕ ਨਿਰਧਾਰਿਤ ਕ੍ਰਮ ਵਿਚ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
rehras.deeperEn: The SGPC sequence opens with nine hymns that praise the One and reflect on Naam and life. It moves to Benti Chaupai’s supplication, an evening Savaiya and Dohira, six selected Anand pauris, and Mundawani and the Mahla 5 Slok. Each part retains its own source family; a single blanket translation would obscure those transitions. Some communities use an extended Rehras sequence, which must be a named separate version.
words: That doorway or court; a poetic question in the opening
Supplication; kept as a companion practice
rehras.caution: This reader follows a specifically bounded SGPC six-part digital source candidate. Additional Rehras passages and precise original-source spellings remain under review; mixed Dasam/SGGS verses are not all on a single SGGS Ang.
rehras.reflection: At the end of the day, what can we carry forward with gratitude, and what should we release?
rehras.question: Why is Rehras studied as a collection with multiple authors and source families?

sohila.theme: Ending the day with remembrance, wonder and humility
sohila.simpleEn: Kirtan Sohila is a five-shabad night prayer. Its images range from songs of joyful union and the changing seasons to the sky as a vast act of praise. It reminds us that life is limited and that remembrance, service and humility matter now.
sohila.simplePa: ਕੀਰਤਨ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਰਾਤ ਦੀ ਪੰਜ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਵਾਲੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਵਿਚ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ, ਮਿਲਾਪ ਦਾ ਪਿਆਰ, ਕੁਦਰਤ ਦੀ ਆਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਅਸਥਿਰਤਾ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਹੈ। ਰਾਤ ਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਟਿਕਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।
sohila.deeperEn: The five shabads move through distinct images: a song of praise, many approaches pointing toward the One, the cosmos as an offering, the challenge of anger and desire, and the urgency of using life well. It is not accurate to flatten all five into the same single “sleep well” message. Their printed raags and Guru attributions belong to the original source metadata, not to claims about one mandatory recording style.
words: Song of joy or praise, with wedding-song imagery
Ceremonial offering or praise; cosmic imagery in Shabad 3
sohila.caution: Five shabads by Guru Nanak, Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan. Wedding and death imagery in the first shabad needs careful cultural interpretation; do not turn this into supernatural or medical claims.
sohila.reflection: What part of today deserves gratitude, and what matters enough not to postpone?
sohila.question: How does Sohila move from songs of celebration to remembering that time is limited?

simple.en: In a place where the Creator is remembered and discussed, sing a song of praise. The shabad uses wedding and departure imagery to ask us to remember the One while life is here.
simple.pa: ਜਿੱਥੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਤੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਉੱਥੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦੇ ਗੀਤ ਗਾਓ। ਵਿਆਹ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਛੋੜੇ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਸੀਮਾ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Praise, meeting and the limits of a human lifetime.
study.closeReading: The first lines invite praise in the company of others; later images of an appointed day and an invitation deepen the meaning. The wedding imagery holds both joy and awareness of departure. The repeated request is to remember the Giver, not to predict when a person will die.
study.interpretationCare: Professor Sahib Singh discusses the cultural wedding-song image. Marriage language is poetic, not a literal claim that a reader is getting married.
study.reflection: What song or remembrance would you want to carry into life’s uncertain moments?
study.teachBack: How can a song contain both joy and a reminder that our time is limited?

simple.en: People may teach in different ways, yet the shabad points toward the One beneath those varied approaches. As seasons and calendars change under one sun, the Creator is not confined to one outward system.
simple.pa: ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਤੇ ਰਾਹ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਹੋ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਬਾਣੀ ਇੱਕੋ ਮੂਲ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਦਿਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇੱਕ ਸੂਰਜ ਹੇਠ ਰੁੱਤਾਂ ਤੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਬਦਲਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Many teachings, one underlying Source.
study.closeReading: Notice the references to six schools and different forms of instruction. The shabad then turns from cataloguing them to its refrain about praise of the Creator. The image of one sun and many seasons helps the learner grasp diversity without losing the unity being praised.
study.interpretationCare: This should not be taught as proof that every religious doctrine is identical. The shabad makes a poetic point with a specific historical image.
study.reflection: When have different descriptions helped you understand one shared reality?
study.teachBack: What does the image of one sun with many seasons contribute to this shabad?

simple.en: The sky becomes a vast platter, the sun and moon lamps, the stars jewels and the wind a fan. The shabad turns our attention from a limited human ritual toward the whole creation praising the One.
simple.pa: ਆਕਾਸ਼ ਥਾਲ, ਸੂਰਜ-ਚੰਦ ਦੀਵੇ ਅਤੇ ਤਾਰੇ ਮੋਤੀ ਵਰਗੇ ਦਿਸਦੇ ਹਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਰਸਮ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਸਾਰੀ ਕੁਦਰਤ ਨੂੰ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਵਿਚ ਲਿਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The cosmos as a poetic aarti.
study.closeReading: In the opening, familiar elements of ritual are recast as sky, celestial lights, fragrance and wind. The shift is from a small constructed offering to wonder at the vast created world. Later lines ask for the grace that allows remembrance.
study.interpretationCare: This is poetry and devotion, not a literal astrophysical model or a demand to reject every form of congregational worship.
study.reflection: How does looking at the natural world change the size of your gratitude?
study.teachBack: Name three elements of the cosmic aarti and describe what changes when the whole sky becomes the place of praise.

simple.en: The mind can become crowded with desire and anger. The shabad turns toward the Guru, humble fellowship and Naam as a source of steadiness rather than leaving the mind to be ruled by its strongest impulses.
simple.pa: ਕਾਮ ਤੇ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਨਾਲ ਮਨ ਭਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਬਾਣੀ ਗੁਰੂ, ਸੰਗਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜ ਕੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੇ ਭਟਕਾਅ ਤੋਂ ਟਿਕਾਉ ਲੱਭਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: From inner turmoil toward spiritual support.
study.closeReading: The opening names desire and anger; the succeeding language of bowing and seeking the holy congregation is a change of posture. The emphasis is on moving away from self-importance toward remembrance and disciplined humility.

words.workingGloss: Holy person or company in context

study.interpretationCare: Do not diagnose ordinary feelings as disease or use this shabad to shame someone for experiencing emotion. It calls for a transformed response.
study.reflection: What helps you respond with steadiness when anger first rises?
study.teachBack: What changes between the opening image of a crowded inner city and the later request for Naam?

simple.en: Life is passing day by day; this shabad asks us not to waste the opportunity for remembrance and service. Its closing prayer seeks humility among those who live close to the Divine.
simple.pa: ਦਿਨ ਰਾਤ ਨਾਲ ਉਮਰ ਘਟਦੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਸ਼ਬਦ ਯਾਦ ਦਿਵਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਸੇਵਾ, ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਹੁਣ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Life’s urgency, service and humility.
study.closeReading: The opening invites friends to listen because this is the time to serve. The phrase about day and night passing is followed by a request to put life’s purpose in order through the Guru. The ending seeks to be dust of the feet of the saintly: an image of radical humility.
study.interpretationCare: Do not read the passing of time as a reason for panic or as a prediction about lifespan; this is a call to meaningful practice.
study.reflection: Which act of care is worth doing today rather than postponing?
study.teachBack: Why does the last shabad place service and humility next to awareness of time?

simple.en: The speaker has seen many disciplined religious paths, yet says that outward learning and practice cannot replace even a tiny measure of divine grace and loving connection.
simple.pa: ਅਨੇਕ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਰਾਹਾਂ ਤੇ ਤਪੱਸਿਆ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਅਤੇ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਦਿਖਾਵਾ ਕਾਫ਼ੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: The limit of outward discipline.
study.closeReading: The stanza lists practitioners and approaches to spiritual life before changing emphasis to divine grace. The contrast asks how much outward effort accomplishes if the heart remains unchanged.
study.interpretationCare: This is an interpretive overview; it is not a rejection of all sincere spiritual disciplines.
study.reflection: What inward quality should accompany a spiritual routine?
study.teachBack: What is the stanza comparing with divine grace?

simple.en: Even royal splendour, decorated elephants and powerful possessions are temporary. They cannot be carried with us at the end of life.
simple.pa: ਰਾਜਸੀ ਠਾਠ ਤੇ ਧਨ-ਦੌਲਤ ਵੀ ਅਸਥਿਰ ਹਨ। ਅੰਤ ਵੇਲੇ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਖਾਲੀ ਹੱਥ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Power and wealth cannot remove impermanence.
study.closeReading: The images of decorated royal life culminate in a stark closing contrast: however mighty a ruler, the person departs without those possessions.
study.interpretationCare: The stanza is not a claim that poverty is automatically virtuous. It asks what wealth can and cannot do.
study.reflection: What do I value that cannot be purchased?
study.teachBack: How does the closing image challenge the opening display of royal power?

simple.en: Conquering territories and receiving public acclaim does not make a life spiritually complete. The stanza asks what remains when victory and recognition end.
simple.pa: ਦੇਸ ਜਿੱਤਣਾ ਜਾਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਾਹ-ਵਾਹ ਹਾਸਲ ਕਰਨੀ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਮੰਜ਼ਿਲ ਨਹੀਂ। ਬਾਣੀ ਪੁੱਛਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਕੀ ਰਹਿ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Military triumph contrasted with divine remembrance.
study.closeReading: Drums and victory announce human power; the last line points back to remembrance of the One. The argument builds through contrast rather than a literal military instruction.
study.interpretationCare: Historical martial imagery is descriptive and theological; it is not permission for present-day violence.
study.reflection: When can recognition distract from why we began a task?
study.teachBack: What is contrasted with the noise of victory?

simple.en: Pilgrimage, charity and self-restraint appear in this stanza, but outward acts by themselves do not replace sincere inner devotion.
simple.pa: ਤੀਰਥ, ਦਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਜਮ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਕੇ ਬਾਣੀ ਦਿਲ ਦੀ ਸਚੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Religious activity and inward orientation.
study.closeReading: The list of commendable practices is deliberately expansive. The final comparison asks the reader whether method and display have displaced the purpose of devotion.
study.interpretationCare: Avoid teaching that seva, charity or ethical restraint are worthless. The passage questions relying solely on their external form.
study.reflection: How can generosity stay sincere when nobody sees it?
study.teachBack: What is missing when a ritual becomes only a public display?

simple.en: The stanza uses armed strength and a formidable army to remind us that even forceful worldly protection has limits; the deepest shelter is not military power alone.
simple.pa: ਤਾਕਤਵਰ ਫੌਜਾਂ ਤੇ ਹਥਿਆਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਬਾਣੀ ਦੱਸਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਬਾਹਰਲੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਸਦਾ ਦਾ ਆਸਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: The limits of physical power.
study.closeReading: The forceful names and descriptions of warriors give way to the reality of leaving the world. The stanza asks where ultimate reliance belongs.
study.interpretationCare: Do not turn spiritual dependence into an argument against responsible self-defence, safety or care.
study.reflection: What helps me remain responsible while remembering my limits?
study.teachBack: What does the final line add after all the military images?

simple.en: Strong warriors and impressive feats are placed beside the One who remains the source of gifts for countless seekers.
simple.pa: ਬਹਾਦਰ ਯੋਧਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਜਿਸ ਕੋਲ ਅਨੇਕ ਮੰਗਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Human courage and the Divine as giver.
study.closeReading: The stanza’s bold imagery should be read as a contrast of scale: remarkable people remain dependent on something greater than their strength.
study.interpretationCare: Some unusual historical words need qualified Dasam Bani grammar review before exact translation.
study.reflection: How is courage different from believing oneself all-powerful?
study.teachBack: Who is presented as the source of gifts beyond human strength?

simple.en: The stanza describes many kinds of beings across time and turns the reader toward the One who is not restricted to one generation or realm.
simple.pa: ਅਤੀਤ, ਵਰਤਮਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਭਵਿੱਖ ਦੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਕੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਇੱਕ ਅਕਾਲ ਸਰੋਤ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Remembrance extends beyond one time and group.
study.closeReading: Notice the widening circles of beings and time. The text invites awe but should not be forced into a literal modern taxonomy of supernatural creatures.
study.interpretationCare: Mythic or cosmic lists in devotional poetry are not evidence of particular physical creatures.
study.reflection: What changes when my perspective expands beyond my own generation?
study.teachBack: How does the stanza widen the circle of remembrance?

simple.en: Even rulers of vast kingdoms are subject to limits. The stanza turns attention from rank and power to the grace of the One.
simple.pa: ਤਿੰਨ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਵਰਗੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਵੀ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਸਹਾਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ। ਧਿਆਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਵੱਲ ਹੈ।

study.focus: No earthly status is permanent.
study.closeReading: Titles of kings and cosmic rulership build the comparison; then grace becomes the decisive term. Its images should be read in their poetic register.
study.interpretationCare: Do not read this as a guarantee of literal immortality for anyone who says particular words.
study.reflection: What is more enduring than a title?
study.teachBack: How do kings and rulers function in the stanza’s contrast?

simple.en: Closing the eyes or performing impressive austerities is not the same as loving union with the Divine. The stanza states its main emphasis clearly: love matters.
simple.pa: ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਅੱਖਾਂ ਮੀਟ ਕੇ ਬੈਠਣਾ ਜਾਂ ਕਠਨ ਤਪ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੀ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਨਹੀਂ। ਬਾਣੀ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਨੂੰ ਮੂਲ ਗੱਲ ਵਜੋਂ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The decisive place of love.
study.closeReading: The image of a motionless person or crane-like display introduces a criticism of outward piety. The closing declaration about prem is the interpretive pivot of the ten Savaiye.
study.interpretationCare: The text does not make sincere meditation wrong; it warns against confusing posture with the inner relationship.
study.reflection: Can love be recognized in daily conduct rather than just an appearance?
study.teachBack: What does the final declaration add to the critique of outward stillness?

simple.en: This stanza compares different objects and forms of worship and warns that external symbols by themselves do not ensure insight into the One.
simple.pa: ਪੂਜਾ ਦੇ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਚਿੰਨ੍ਹ ਤੇ ਰੀਤਾਂ ਦਿਖਾਏ ਗਏ ਹਨ। ਬਾਣੀ ਯਾਦ ਦਿਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਚਿੰਨ੍ਹ ਹੀ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦੇ।

study.focus: Distinguishing sacred objects from inner insight.
study.closeReading: Several ritual forms appear in rapid succession before the closing reflection on not discerning the Divine. The learner should see the original terms and consider the context rather than using a short overview to insult others.

words.workingGloss: Ritual action presented critically in context

study.interpretationCare: This wording refers to historical religious practices. Do not repurpose the lesson to mock neighbours or other faith communities.
study.reflection: Where does a meaningful symbol help me, and where can it become an empty substitute?
study.teachBack: How does the final line relate to the objects listed earlier?

simple.en: The One cannot be confined to caste, colour, shape, clothing or a visible mark. Human language may praise, but it cannot completely describe the Divine.
simple.pa: ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਤ, ਰੰਗ, ਆਕਾਰ ਜਾਂ ਭੇਖ ਵਿਚ ਕੈਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ। ਅਸੀਂ ਗੁਣ ਗਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਪਰ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੰਨ੍ਹ ਸਕਦੇ।

study.focus: Beyond human labels and descriptions.
study.closeReading: The opening names common human ways of classifying a person, then denies that any can enclose the Divine. The final question about the One’s names opens the long sequence of praise that follows.

words.workingGloss: Self-existent or beyond ordinary apprehension; verify grammar

study.interpretationCare: Jaap is multilingual poetry. The opening is not a license to erase human experiences of caste injustice; it calls into question imposing limiting labels on the One.
study.reflection: What changes when I resist reducing anyone to a label?
study.teachBack: Why does the poem ask how the many names could all be told?

simple.en: The repeated salutations remember the timeless, compassionate, formless and incomparable One.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਿਆਂ ਅਕਾਲ, ਕਿਰਪਾਲ, ਅਰੂਪ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੂਪ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Four names that work together.
study.closeReading: The repetition makes each word a new focus for attention. Timelessness and compassion stand next to formlessness and incomparability, rather than suggesting four different divine beings.
study.interpretationCare: These are close working glosses; the morphology, pronunciation and metre still require qualified review.
study.reflection: Which attribute opens a question rather than merely giving you an answer?
study.teachBack: What is the function of repeating ਨਮਸਤੰ?

simple.en: The salutation continues: the One cannot be contained in ordinary appearance, depiction, body or birth.
simple.pa: ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਲੜੀ ਵਿਚ ਰੂਪ, ਲਿਖਤ, ਦੇਹ ਅਤੇ ਜਨਮ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The Divine is more than what can be represented.
study.closeReading: Short rhythmical expressions give the mind something to hold while pointing to what those expressions cannot capture. Study these in their context, without inventing a detailed biological claim.
study.interpretationCare: A poetic denial of bodily limits is not a testable claim about human physiology.
study.reflection: When can a picture help understanding, and when can it mislead?
study.teachBack: How does this chhand extend the first chhand’s refusal of fixed appearance?

simple.en: The One is praised as not subject to ordinary destruction, not captured by one assigned name or fixed place.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਵਿਚ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਨਾਸ, ਇੱਕੋ ਨਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਇੱਕੋ ਥਾਂ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ।

study.focus: No final container for the One.
study.closeReading: The rhythm repeats several negative attributes. Their shared poetic movement is to remove limitations rather than offer competing portraits of the Divine.

words.workingGloss: Unconquered or indestructible, pending exact gloss

study.interpretationCare: Word roots and specific translations must be checked against a Dasam Bani glossary, not generated from superficial similarities.
study.reflection: Which label do you treat as more final than it should be?
study.teachBack: What do the repeated negatives teach about trying to define the One?

simple.en: Another set of salutations points beyond ordinary human classifications of action, dwelling and name.
simple.pa: ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਕੰਮ, ਵਸੇਬੇ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਵਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The sequence of words, not isolated labels.
study.closeReading: Chhand 5 continues the rhythm of address. The safest first step is to see its relationship to the surrounding salutations before insisting on a single English meaning for every historically layered term.

words.workingGloss: Not confined to a dwelling, draft gloss

study.interpretationCare: Terms such as ਅਕਰਮੰ and ਅਧਰਮੰ require contextual expert adjudication; the app must not teach an unqualified claim that the Divine is “unethical.”
study.reflection: Can a term mean something different in devotional poetry than in daily speech?
study.teachBack: How does the larger sequence keep a single ambiguous word from being misunderstood?

simple.en: The One is saluted as unconquered and beyond fear or injury; the language expresses trust rather than human invulnerability.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਅਜਿੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਡਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਨੂੰ ਅਜਿੱਤ ਬਣਨ ਦੀ ਗਾਰੰਟੀ ਨਹੀਂ, ਭਰੋਸੇ ਦੀ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Courageful names of the One.
study.closeReading: Words associated with defeat and fear carry devotional force here. The surrounding salutation sequence keeps the praise directed to the Divine rather than a mortal warrior.
study.interpretationCare: Do not claim that reciting these words prevents physical injury. Pronunciation and nuanced lexicon remain review-needed.
study.reflection: How can faith support courage without denying real danger?
study.teachBack: Whose qualities are being praised in these four lines?

simple.en: The One is remembered as without beginning and beyond ordinary cutting or measuring, extending the image of the limitless.
simple.pa: ਉਹ ਇੱਕ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਪ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ। ਸ਼ਬਦ ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Beginningless and unfathomable praise.
study.closeReading: The opening chhands cumulatively build a language of awe. Rather than memorizing unreviewed word lists, compare their shared movement from human limits toward the One beyond them.
study.interpretationCare: Some nearby source spellings and phonemes vary across digital transcriptions; santhiya remains a separate human-led task.
study.reflection: What does awe feel like when you accept that your knowledge is incomplete?
study.teachBack: What has changed from Jaap’s first chhand to this set of salutations?

simple.en: The opening asks the Divine to protect the speaker, guide the mind and keep it close in humble refuge.
simple.pa: ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ। ਮਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਰਹੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਆਪਣੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰੇ।

study.focus: Protection joined to inner orientation.
study.closeReading: The request for safety sits beside a request about where the mind should remain. This is more than a demand for a particular outcome; the speaker asks to live in relationship with the Divine.
study.interpretationCare: A prayer for protection is not a promise that hardships never happen.
study.reflection: How can seeking safety and seeking a steadier mind belong together?
study.teachBack: Where in the first pauri does the prayer move from protection to relationship?

simple.en: The prayer asks for defence against harm and wellbeing for one’s family and community.
simple.pa: ਬੇਨਤੀ ਵਿਚ ਦੁੱਖ ਤੇ ਵੈਰ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਨਾਲ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਸੇਵਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੁਖ-ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਵੀ ਮੰਗੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Protection of self and community.
study.closeReading: The movement expands from “me” to family and other servants or Sikhs. It is meaningful to study this communal scope alongside the martial language rather than isolating one aggressive phrase.
study.interpretationCare: Language about destroying enemies belongs to a particular literary and historical context. Do not use a devotional lesson to label actual neighbours as enemies or excuse violence.
study.reflection: Whose safety do I include when I pray for my own?
study.teachBack: What does the stanza ask for beyond the speaker alone?

simple.en: The speaker asks for help against danger and for a lasting thirst for divine remembrance.
simple.pa: ਸੰਕਟ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਭਜਨ ਦੀ ਪਿਆਸ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿਣ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਵੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Courage and remembrance.
study.closeReading: The final request for longing toward devotion gives direction to the earlier images of protection. Learning should preserve both the martial and inward language.
study.interpretationCare: The image of a “foe” should not be automatically converted into a diagnosis of someone’s psychology.
study.reflection: What kind of longing would help direct your actions?
study.teachBack: How does the final line reshape the earlier appeal for protection?

simple.en: The speaker pledges reliance on the One and asks that the community be carried through danger.
simple.pa: ਬਾਣੀ ਵਿਚ ਹੋਰ ਆਸਰਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਉੱਤੇ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Exclusive reliance and responsibility.
study.closeReading: The pauri places trust and a plea for others side by side. Martial expressions are present, but a learning application should not flatten them into an invitation to personal aggression.
study.interpretationCare: The boundaries of historically contextual enemy-language need qualified literary review.
study.reflection: What does loyalty to the One look like in the way I treat others?
study.teachBack: What are the two kinds of requests in this pauri?

simple.en: The prayer asks the Divine to remain close through fear, even the fear of death.
simple.pa: ਮੌਤ ਦੇ ਡਰ ਸਮੇਤ ਹਰ ਸੰਕਟ ਵੇਲੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Protection through mortality.
study.closeReading: The appeal becomes more personal: the speaker asks to be lifted up when afraid. It expresses dependence and hope, not an empirically guaranteed escape from danger.
study.interpretationCare: Do not tell vulnerable people that danger can be ignored because the prayer has been recited.
study.reflection: What support helps a person face fear more wisely?
study.teachBack: How does this pauri describe the speaker’s relationship to fear?

simple.en: The Divine is addressed as protector, helper of the humble and Sovereign beyond ordinary limits.
simple.pa: ਰੱਖਣਹਾਰ, ਦੀਨਬੰਧੂ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਕੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਮੰਗੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Names of shelter and sovereignty.
study.closeReading: Each title develops the speaker’s trust in the One. The phrase about the fourteen realms is a traditional cosmic image of breadth, not modern astronomical measurement.
study.interpretationCare: Treat cosmic imagery as poetry in its historical context, not a scientific map.
study.reflection: Whom do I need to include in the care shown to the lowly?
study.teachBack: How do the various titles expand the idea of protection?

simple.en: The stanza places famous figures of traditional cosmology inside time, while pointing beyond them toward the One.
simple.pa: ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾ, ਸ਼ਿਵ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਨੂ ਦੇ ਨਾਮ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਵੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੇ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਸਲ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The changing within time and the One beyond it.
study.closeReading: The names of divine figures are used within the poem’s traditional vocabulary. The important comparison is that manifestations occur in time; do not collapse the imagery into a literal historical timetable.
study.interpretationCare: This is a theological poem, not data proving a precise age of the universe.
study.reflection: What helps me remember that even impressive systems change?
study.teachBack: What contrast does the repetition of ਕਾਲ create?

simple.en: The opening celebrates a kind of bliss connected with finding the True Guru. The mind feels a deep, natural song of joy through the Guru’s Sabad.
simple.pa: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਪਉੜੀ ਵਿਚ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਨੂੰ ਪਾ ਕੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਅਨੰਦ ਉਪਜਣ ਦੀ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਹੈ। ਮਨ ਵਿਚ ਸਹਜ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਵੱਜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Joy as encounter with the Guru’s wisdom.
study.closeReading: The opening addresses the speaker’s mother in intimate language. The discovery of the Satiguru leads to a celebration in the mind. The imagery of instruments and song should not be reduced to an external concert alone.
study.interpretationCare: SikhRI interprets this as durable bliss rather than fleeting pleasure. Treat the educational comparison as interpretation, not a promise of constant happy emotions.
study.reflection: What is different between excitement and a grounded sense of joy?
study.teachBack: Why does the Guru appear in the first and final lines of this pauri?

simple.en: The speaker addresses the mind: stay connected to the Divine and do not forget the source of comfort and guidance.
simple.pa: ਆਪਣੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ: ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਰਹੁ, ਉਸ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਵਿਸਾਰ।

study.focus: A direct conversation with the mind.
study.closeReading: The word “mind” at the opening makes this intimate rather than abstract. The invitation to remain with the One and move through sorrow sits in a larger teaching of remembrance, not a demand to hide feelings.
study.interpretationCare: It should not be presented as clinical treatment for sadness or a promise that grief cannot occur.
study.reflection: What gentle reminder would you give your mind at a difficult moment?
study.teachBack: To whom does the speaker speak, and what is repeatedly requested?

simple.en: Everything the speaker truly needs is held within the True One. The pauri turns from asking for things to cultivating praise and Naam within the mind.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚੇ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਕੋਲ ਘਾਟ ਨਹੀਂ। ਪਉੜੀ ਮੰਗਣ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਮਨ ਵਿਚ ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਵਸਾਉਣ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Abundance and gratitude.
study.closeReading: The repeated rhetorical question emphasizes the Giver’s abundance. The movement toward praise and Naam keeps this from becoming simply a request for material benefits.
study.interpretationCare: A phrase about the One having everything is not a guarantee that every personal wish is granted.
study.reflection: What can gratitude change even before circumstances change?
study.teachBack: How does the pauri connect abundance to remembrance?

simple.en: True Naam is described as the speaker’s support, easing the hunger of craving and bringing inward calm.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚਾ ਨਾਮ ਆਸਰਾ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ; ਤ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨਾ ਦੀ ਭੁੱਖ ਘਟਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A source of steadiness stronger than craving.
study.closeReading: The repeated refrain of Naam as support frames the movement. The pauri uses inner hunger and contentment imagery rather than prescribing a dietary practice.
study.interpretationCare: Do not confuse metaphorical hunger here with physical starvation or make claims about medical appetite control.
study.reflection: Where does wanting more make it harder to notice what is enough?
study.teachBack: Which recurring phrase tells you what the speaker relies upon?

simple.en: The fortunate inner home resounds with Sabad. The stanza describes freedom from impulses that once overpowered the mind.
simple.pa: ਮਨ ਦੇ ਸੁਭਾਗੇ ਘਰ ਵਿਚ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦੀ ਧੁਨ ਹੈ। ਅੰਦਰਲੇ ਵਿਕਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੱਸ ਘਟਣ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Inner music and transformation.
study.closeReading: The poetic language of five sounds, the five troublemakers and unstruck melody expresses a transformed spiritual condition. It belongs to Gurbani’s symbolism of the mind, not a numerical recipe.

words.workingGloss: Five sounds or forms in a symbolic context

study.interpretationCare: No specific sound frequency, neurological mechanism or promised effect is established by this metaphor.
study.reflection: What habits lose strength when attention grows steadier?
study.teachBack: How does the imagery of music describe an inner transformation?

simple.en: Without a sincere connection to the One, the body’s life feels spiritually unsupported; the speaker asks for grace and the guidance of Sabad.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚੀ ਲਿਵ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਜੀਵਨ ਅੰਦਰੋਂ ਅਧੂਰਾ ਮਹਿਸੂਸ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਬਾਣੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਤੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The importance of a sustained orientation.
study.closeReading: The refrain about the body lacking liv makes an interior point through physical language. The request for grace gives the stanza the character of prayer rather than condemnation.
study.interpretationCare: Do not imply that anyone without religious practice has no dignity or medical worth.
study.reflection: What helps bring your attention back to what matters?
study.teachBack: What is being asked for after naming the absence of liv?

simple.en: Many people speak about happiness, but this pauri says the deeper Anand is learned through the Guru’s wisdom and a loosening of attachment.
simple.pa: ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਸਭ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਅਸਲ ਅਨੰਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਤੇ ਮੋਹ ਦੇ ਘਟਣ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Naming joy versus understanding it.
study.closeReading: The stanza repeats “anand” before explaining that the Guru reveals its meaning. The line about applying the salve of knowledge connects inner vision with release from attachment.

words.workingGloss: The salve of wisdom; poetic eye-image

study.interpretationCare: Do not equate ordinary joyful emotions with moral failure; this pauri speaks about depth and direction.
study.reflection: What kind of happiness remains meaningful during a difficult season?
study.teachBack: Why does the pauri repeat the word anand before explaining it?

simple.en: So Dar asks what kind of Divine court or presence holds the world. Wind, water, fire, musicians and beings become part of a vast language of praise.
simple.pa: ਸੋ ਦਰ ਪੁੱਛਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦਾ ਦਰ ਕਿਹੋ ਜਿਹਾ ਹੈ। ਪਵਣ, ਪਾਣੀ, ਅੱਗ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਜੀਵ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਗਾਉਂਦੇ ਦਿਖਾਏ ਗਏ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The uncountable court of the One.
study.closeReading: The hymn answers its own question through an ever-expanding roll call of creation. The repeated praise of the One is far wider than a single palace or music performance.
study.interpretationCare: Cosmic praise is poetic and theological. Do not present it as evidence of literally audible planets or wind.
study.reflection: How does the hymn help you notice things bigger than yourself?
study.teachBack: Why does the list of singers keep expanding?

simple.en: The True One is so deep and vast that the speaker cannot measure or price that greatness. Praise continues even when explanation reaches its limits.
simple.pa: ਸੱਚੇ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈ; ਮਨੁੱਖ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਮੋਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾ ਸਕਦਾ। ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਜਾਰੀ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The limits of measuring greatness.
study.closeReading: A repeated question about size and value is a way of expressing wonder. The poem does not reject understanding; it recognizes its boundaries.
study.interpretationCare: Do not translate metaphorical greatness into literal physical height or mass.
study.reflection: Where can humility improve the quality of understanding?
study.teachBack: What repeated question shows the difficulty of describing the One?

simple.en: Naam is so precious that losing remembrance feels like losing life’s direction. The hymn asks how the true Giver could be forgotten.
simple.pa: ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਲੋੜ ਵਾਂਗ ਦੱਸੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ। ਸੱਚੇ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਭੁਲਾਈਏ—ਇਹ ਮੁੱਖ ਪੁਕਾਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Remembrance as spiritual nourishment.
study.closeReading: The language of hunger and life is intense. Its central idea is longing for Naam and recognition of the Giver, not a medical statement about breathing or survival.

words.workingGloss: I live through remembrance/praise, working gloss

study.interpretationCare: Do not convert spiritual metaphor into advice to skip food or treatment.
study.reflection: What do you return to when attention scatters?
study.teachBack: How does hunger imagery make remembrance feel urgent?

simple.en: The speaker asks the Guru for the light of Naam. The hymn places humility and sangat at the centre of a daily path.
simple.pa: ਗੁਰੂ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਾਮ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਮੰਗਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਰਾਹ ਵਿਚ ਮਹੱਤਵ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Naam through Guru and community.
study.closeReading: The hymn includes the word ਰਹਰਾਸਿ in the source. See how supplication, teaching and community become connected; the concept is richer than a time slot.

words.workingGloss: Daily path or devotional practice in context

study.interpretationCare: An authoritative linguistic interpretation of this historical term needs source-specific review.
study.reflection: How can good company support a difficult habit?
study.teachBack: What is the speaker asking of the Guru?

simple.en: Why be consumed by worry when the Giver sustains creation? The hymn counsels remembrance and trust through images from animals and the natural world.
simple.pa: ਜਦੋਂ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਮਨ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਵਿਚ ਕਿਉਂ ਡੁੱਬੇ? ਸ਼ਬਦ ਕੁਦਰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਮਿਸਾਲਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਸਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Trust without abandoning responsibility.
study.closeReading: Natural-world examples show care for small beings. The point is an invitation to trust and remembrance, not an instruction to avoid earning, feeding family or making responsible plans.
study.interpretationCare: Never use this lesson to tell someone to neglect finances, nutrition or medical needs.
study.reflection: Can trust make you more responsible rather than less?
study.teachBack: Why does the shabad use small creatures to illustrate care?

simple.en: So Purakh praises the One as the source of all beings and the giver of life; the hymn repeatedly draws attention beyond the individual.
simple.pa: ਸੋ ਪੁਰਖ ਵਿਚ ਸਾਰੇ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ। ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਸਾਡਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The Giver of all life.
study.closeReading: Repeated address to Hari and the Creator ties together the world, the devotee and the possibility of remembrance. The cosmic language encourages gratitude and humility.
study.interpretationCare: Terms for the Divine are understood in a Sikh theological setting and must not be used to make all traditions identical.
study.reflection: How might gratitude change the way you treat another being?
study.teachBack: Which repeated phrases hold the hymn together?

simple.en: Human life is presented as a precious opportunity to meet the Divine through Naam and sangat. The call is to make meaningful use of this chance.
simple.pa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾ ਜੀਵਨ ਨੂੰ ਕੀਮਤੀ ਮੌਕਾ ਕਿਹਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਨਾਮ ਤੇ ਸੰਗਤ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਇਸ ਮੌਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਰਥਕ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਪੁਕਾਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The preciousness of this life.
study.closeReading: The opening “ਭਈ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਮਾਨੁਖ ਦੇਹੁਰੀਆ” establishes urgency. The following image of crossing life’s ocean broadens the meaning beyond the pursuit of short-lived rewards.
study.interpretationCare: Urgency is not permission to threaten or frighten children about death or afterlife.
study.reflection: What is worth doing with the opportunity of today?
study.teachBack: What does the hymn call the human body, and what responsibility follows?

simple.en: The evening prayer turns from SGGS hymns to Benti Chaupai’s appeal for protection and steady devotion.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਰਹਿਰਾਸਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਚੌਪਈ ਦੇ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਵਾਲੇ ਸੁਰ ਵਿਚ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A change of source family and prayer voice.
study.closeReading: The Benti Chaupai excerpt is a Dasam Bani segment, not an SGGS verse. The learner should see both the source change and the continuity of remembrance and trust.
study.interpretationCare: Our 25-pauri evening excerpt is distinct from the expanded 29-pauri morning digital candidate.
study.reflection: How does prayer sound different when it turns to a direct plea?
study.teachBack: Which source family begins at this passage?

simple.en: The evening Savaiya speaks of relying on the Divine rather than dividing one’s allegiance among competing descriptions and books.
simple.pa: ਸ਼ਾਮ ਦੇ ਸਵੱਯੇ ਵਿਚ ਸਾਰਾ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਦਰ ਵੱਲ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: One source of reliance despite many labels.
study.closeReading: This is the Pae Gahe Savaiya, not one of the ten Sravag Sudh morning Savaiye. It uses historically layered references to traditions and sacred books while making a devotional statement of dependence.
study.interpretationCare: Do not use references to named traditions to insult their followers; qualified religious-linguistic review remains necessary.
study.reflection: What is the difference between openness to learning and losing one’s own grounding?
study.teachBack: Why must this evening Savaiya not be confused with the ten morning Savaiye?

simple.en: The Dohira asks for refuge at the One’s doorway, using the image of holding the protective hand of the Divine.
simple.pa: ਦੋਹਿਰੇ ਵਿਚ ਹੋਰ ਦਰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਦਰ ਨੂੰ ਫੜਨ ਦੀ ਨਿਮਰ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Refuge and commitment.
study.closeReading: The very short form concentrates the preceding appeal into a memorable image of one doorway and faithful dependence.
study.interpretationCare: Do not literalize the doorway as one physical building; it is devotional imagery.
study.reflection: What does it mean to seek guidance rather than control every outcome?
study.teachBack: Which image carries the meaning of refuge in the Dohira?

simple.en: Rehras now selects Anand Sahib’s first five and last pauri, carrying the theme of deep joy into the evening sequence.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਰਹਿਰਾਸਿ ਵਿਚ ਅਨੰਦੁ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀਆਂ ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਪੰਜ ਅਤੇ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਪਉੜੀ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਅਨੰਦ ਦਾ ਸੁਰ ਸ਼ਾਮ ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਵਿਚ ਜੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A source-bound return to Anand.
study.closeReading: The selected Anand verses have their own SGGS source, even when included inside the mixed Rehras order. Study the complete Anand Sahib separately to understand the full forty-pauri argument.
study.interpretationCare: This is a selection, not a new authorship or a replacement for all forty Anand pauris.
study.reflection: How does the feeling of evening prayer change when these verses begin?
study.teachBack: Which pauris of Anand are included here?

simple.en: The selected concluding Anand pauri returns to blessings, hearing true bani and the completion of the inner search.
simple.pa: ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਚਾਲੀਵੀਂ ਪਉੜੀ ਸੱਚੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਸੁਣਨ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੇ ਸੁਖ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਨਾਲ ਇਹ ਭਾਗ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Completion in the selected Anand portion.
study.closeReading: The final pauri belongs to Anand Sahib and closes the shortened Rehras selection. Read it with the first five, without pretending the intervening thirty-four pauris were not part of the complete bani.
study.interpretationCare: Expressions about pain and illness in devotional verse should not be marketed as guaranteed medical treatment.
study.reflection: What would it mean to listen with attention rather than rush?
study.teachBack: Why is the last pauri selected alongside the first five?

simple.en: Mundawani uses the image of a platter containing truth, contentment and reflection, with Naam as nourishing sustenance.
simple.pa: ਮੁੰਦਾਵਣੀ ਵਿਚ ਥਾਲ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਨਾਲ ਸਤ, ਸੰਤੋਖ, ਵਿਚਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰੂਪੀ ਦਾਤ ਸਮਝਾਈ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Nourishment through truth, contentment and reflection.
study.closeReading: The imagery names qualities that belong together. This is a spiritual platter, not a dietary plan or literal claim about nutritional contents.
study.interpretationCare: Modern comparisons with mindfulness or nutrition must be explicitly labeled as our commentary, not source translation.
study.reflection: What quality would you bring to tomorrow’s “platter”?
study.teachBack: What three things appear in the image of the platter?

simple.en: The final Slok is full of gratitude and humility: the speaker recognizes how much the Giver has done and asks for the gift of Naam.
simple.pa: ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਸਲੋਕ ਵਿਚ ਸ਼ੁਕਰਾਨਾ ਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਹੈ। ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਮਿਹਰ ਨੂੰ ਮੰਨ ਕੇ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਦਾਤ ਮੰਗੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Ending with gratitude rather than entitlement.
study.closeReading: The opening “ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਤੋ ਨਾਹੀ” marks the tone. The speaker sees grace not as a prize earned by moral superiority but as something received with humility.
study.interpretationCare: Avoid the idea that gratitude should silence someone facing harm or needing support.
study.reflection: What can you acknowledge as a gift without denying today’s difficulties?
study.teachBack: How is the Slok’s voice different from a demand for rewards?

simple.en: The poem looks beyond named divine figures to the source that orders and sustains the worlds.
simple.pa: ਬਾਣੀ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਪੁਰਾਣਕ ਪਾਤਰਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਸਰੋਤ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The creative power beyond familiar images.
study.closeReading: The sequence begins with Shiva as yogi and Brahma in relation to the Vedas, then widens to all worlds. Its closing salutation makes the object of devotion clearer: not separate historical heroes, but the one Divine Source that exceeds them.

words.workingGloss: That which or the One who; a Braj relative expression

study.interpretationCare: Kaal can mean time or a divine epithet in Dasam poetry; precise morphology and comparison of printed editions are not cleared.
study.reflection: How can recognizing one source deepen respect without disparaging anyone else?
study.teachBack: Where does the fourth line direct the salutation after the first three images?

simple.en: The Creator who fashioned the world and its diverse beings is the same One the poet accepts as Guru.
simple.pa: ਜਿਸ ਇੱਕ ਨੇ ਜਗਤ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਜੀਵ ਰਚੇ ਹਨ, ਕਵੀ ਉਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਮੰਨਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Creation, beginning and the One who guides.
study.closeReading: The first two lines give the breadth of creation by naming the world and traditional classes of beings. The last two turn from diversity to unity: the Divine remains the Source through beginning and end, and the speaker declares that One to be the Guru.

words.workingGloss: Enlightening teacher; the Divine guide in this context

study.interpretationCare: Names for devas, daits and yakshas belong to traditional poetic cosmology; they are not a verified biological catalogue.
study.reflection: Does my sense of guidance rest on forms that change or on principles that endure?
study.teachBack: Why does the poet end a list of created beings with “That is my Guru”?

simple.en: The speaker offers salutations to the Creator who sustains beings and stands with devotees.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਸਹਾਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: From gratitude for creation to protection.
study.closeReading: This pauri begins with a direct act of praise, names the Divine as maker of all people and ends with sharply drawn distinctions between care for devotees and defeat of hostile forces. Reading the whole unit avoids isolating the battle image from its prayerful beginning.

words.workingGloss: Good qualities or blessings; working lexical reading

study.interpretationCare: The end uses martial rhetoric; it does not empower a reader to name neighbours as enemies, and no real-world protection outcome is guaranteed.
study.reflection: How can I be grateful for care without treating prayer as a substitute for responsibility?
study.teachBack: What movement occurs between praise in line one and the ending battle imagery?

simple.en: From the smallest to the greatest, the Divine knows every heart and looks upon beings with compassion.
simple.pa: ਨਿੱਕੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਜੀਵ ਤੱਕ ਸਭ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਹਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Universal care and intimate knowledge.
study.closeReading: The poem says “ghat ghat”—heart after heart—before contrasting an ant and elephant. Size and status do not limit attention from the Divine. The final line connects this knowing to compassionate regard, a crucial correction to fear-based readings of omniscience.

words.workingGloss: A vessel; a living body or heart in devotional idiom

study.interpretationCare: Do not claim a human teacher can read another person’s heart because this verse praises Divine knowledge.
study.reflection: Whose pain have I overlooked because they seem unimportant?
study.teachBack: Why does the ant–elephant comparison matter beside “every heart”?

simple.en: The speaker describes a Divine presence attentive to each person’s joy, sorrow and hidden pain.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਹਰ ਜੀਵ ਦੇ ਸੁੱਖ, ਦੁੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਪੀੜ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਦਇਆ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A prayer of empathic awareness.
study.closeReading: The repeated pairs of suffering and happiness build toward “each one’s pain.” The final line deepens the image from outward emotions to the hidden folds within every heart. This is the poem’s language of compassion, not an instruction to read people’s minds.
study.interpretationCare: It does not mean human grief is evidence of failed prayer or that hardship can be prevented by a particular verse.
study.reflection: How might I respond differently when another person is quietly struggling?
study.teachBack: Which phrase in this unit moves from groups of people to each individual?

simple.en: All embodied life comes forth through the Creator and is pictured as returning into that same Source.
simple.pa: ਸਾਰੇ ਜੀਵ ਕਰਤਾਰ ਦੇ ਪਸਾਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੂਪ ਧਾਰਦੇ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਸੇ ਮੂਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਾਉਂਦੇ ਦਿਖਾਏ ਹਨ।

study.focus: The poetic rhythm of manifestation and return.
study.closeReading: The first half imagines expansion or bringing forth of forms; the second imagines contraction or withdrawal. Both describe dependence on the Creator. The paired verbs carry the theological picture, and their exact Braj meanings still need a qualified review.
study.interpretationCare: This is not a scientific cosmology, a measured timeline or a substitute for studying physical origins of life.
study.reflection: Can I value things that change without expecting them to last forever?
study.teachBack: What contrasting actions in lines one and three structure this pauri?

simple.en: Many voices speak of the Creator through their own limits, while the One remains beyond every limited description.
simple.pa: ਮਨੁੱਖ ਆਪਣੇ-ਆਪਣੇ ਗਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਵਰਣਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਇੱਕ ਹਰ ਵਰਣਨ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The humility of partial human descriptions.
study.closeReading: The opening alludes to countless mouths and ways of speaking, then names the bounds of each individual understanding. The turning point is “You remain distinct.” The lesson is not that study is useless, but that honest study remembers its own limits.

words.workingGloss: Face or mouth in this context
Separate, beyond limiting association; working gloss

study.interpretationCare: Do not use the plurality of descriptions as proof that all beliefs or religious communities hold the same teachings.
study.reflection: When has admitting uncertainty improved a conversation?
study.teachBack: Which line stops the many descriptions from becoming a final definition of the One?

simple.en: The One is praised as formless, uncorrupted and beyond the beginning, while human descriptions remain incomplete.
simple.pa: ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ, ਵਿਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਅਤੇ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਮਝ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਸਾਰਾ ਭੇਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਭ ਸਕਦੀ।

study.focus: An accumulation of Divine attributes.
study.closeReading: Two densely packed lines of attributes give way to a warning about making distinctions without knowledge. The closing line notes that even venerable texts cannot exhaust the One’s mystery. This is reverence expressed through language that also confesses language is insufficient.
study.interpretationCare: Individual Sanskritic/Dasam inflections such as nirlambh and asambh require qualified philology; this is not a claim against education.
study.reflection: How can names illuminate a reality without fully containing it?
study.teachBack: Why does a stanza full of names conclude with a warning about naming?

simple.en: The poet criticizes attempts to reduce the formless Divine to one object or familiar named deity.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਇੱਕ ਵਸਤੂ ਜਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਉੱਤੇ ਸਵਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Formless reality and the danger of narrow representation.
study.closeReading: The first two lines speak sharply about making a stone stand for the limitless. The second pair invokes Mahadev and the idea of the Eternal. In its literary setting this is a Sikh theological contrast, not permission to insult any other religion.
study.interpretationCare: This polemical register can be deeply sensitive: avoid stereotyping, insulting people or erasing their religious dignity.
study.reflection: When does a helpful symbol begin to replace what it was meant to remind us of?
study.teachBack: How do the two images in the pauri make one larger argument?

simple.en: People describe the Divine through limited understanding, while the scale and beginnings of creation inspire wonder.
simple.pa: ਹਰ ਕੋਈ ਆਪਣੀ ਸੀਮਤ ਸਮਝ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਵਰਣਦਾ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦਾ ਪਸਾਰਾ ਤੇ ਆਰੰਭ ਅਚਰਜ ਜਗਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Different understandings, one source beyond calculation.
study.closeReading: Line one sets the capacity of each mind; line two explains differing descriptions. The final pair expands the question beyond any individual mind to the vastness and beginning of creation. Rather than refusing knowledge, the speaker asks with humility.

words.workingGloss: Extent, expansion, the breadth of creation

study.interpretationCare: Do not convert the unanswered poetic question into a falsifiable modern scientific hypothesis.
study.reflection: Where could greater curiosity replace my certainty?
study.teachBack: What link connects the limited mind in line one and the question in line four?

simple.en: The One is present through rulers and the humble, and through diverse traditional classes of living beings.
simple.pa: ਉਹ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਰੰਕ, ਰਾਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਰਵਾਇਤੀ ਜਨਮ-ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣਾ ਪਸਾਰਾ ਵਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Seeing beyond social rank and conventional categories.
study.closeReading: The pair of poor and royal points away from judging value through class. The next two lines list familiar “khanis,” traditional categories of life from egg, womb, moisture and plants. Their purpose is to communicate diversity of creation, not biological taxonomy.
study.interpretationCare: The four birth classes are premodern religious categories and do not replace contemporary biological understanding.
study.reflection: How can I treat people with equal dignity despite different social positions?
study.teachBack: How does the shift from poor and king to birth-categories widen the idea of creation?

simple.en: Different conditions and appearances do not limit the timeless One who brings the changing world into view.
simple.pa: ਕਿਤੇ ਰਾਜ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਾਨ ਤੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਸਿਮਟਿਆ ਰੂਪ ਦਿੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਆਪ-ਹੋਂਦ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The movement between forms and the unchanging.
study.closeReading: Two contrasting ways of appearing—expansive royal splendour and a contracted form—are followed by creation’s countless wonders. The final epithet “self-existent through ages” stops any one picture from standing for the Divine as a whole.
study.interpretationCare: The reading of “Sankar” in line two is unsettled without Braj/Dasam source comparison; do not infer a literal transformation timeline.
study.reflection: What can change around me without altering the values that guide me?
study.teachBack: Which word at the end contrasts most strongly with the earlier changing appearances?

simple.en: The speaker petitions for protection during conflict, using severe historic warfare language that requires ethical and textual care.
simple.pa: ਕਵੀ ਲੜਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਕਟ ਵਿਚ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਮੰਗਦਾ ਹੈ; ਤਿੱਖੀ ਵੈਰੀ-ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਨੂੰ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਤੇ ਨੈਤਿਕ ਸੰਦਰਭ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A protective plea, with boundaries on historical polemic.
study.closeReading: The first line asks for personal rescue; the next brings Sikhs into the concern. The final two contain hostile martial terms and ask for defeat of forces causing upheaval. Source-faithful study must acknowledge their intensity while refusing to target any present-day religious or ethnic population.

words.workingGloss: Hostile or harmful person/force in the poem

study.interpretationCare: The expression “malechh” is historically charged and sometimes derogatory. Never treat it as an authorized label for contemporary non-Sikhs or as permission to harm anyone.
study.reflection: How can protection of my community coexist with respect for every human being?
study.teachBack: How does the prayer develop from personal protection to a broader martial plea?

simple.en: The poem honours those who seek shelter in the Divine and asks for their troubles to be lifted.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸੰਕਟ ਦੂਰ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Refuge as a relationship rather than entitlement.
study.closeReading: The two paired lines each identify a seeker and the fate of adversity. “Asidhuj” names the Divine in traditional martial vocabulary. The emphasis of the complete unit is shelter for those who depend upon the One, not power granted to private aggressors.
study.interpretationCare: Do not interpret divine protection as a reason to ignore immediate physical danger or withhold practical support.
study.reflection: What would seeking help responsibly look like in a difficult situation?
study.teachBack: Who seeks shelter in each of the two halves of this pauri?

simple.en: Remembrance is described in powerful images of protection from death, danger and evil.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਵੀ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਲਈ ਕਾਲ ਤੇ ਵੈਰ ਤੋਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਭਗਤੀ-ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Poetic protection without false guarantees.
study.closeReading: The poem uses an intentionally strong progression: one act of remembrance; death kept at a distance; protection through time; danger dispersed. The images communicate profound trust in the Divine. A modern learner must distinguish that spiritual claim from guarantees about bodily survival.

words.workingGloss: The present age, Kaliyug, in devotional time reckoning

study.interpretationCare: Never advertise this verse as preventing death, curing illness, avoiding a car accident or substituting for emergency services.
study.reflection: How can a prayer strengthen courage while I still take sensible precautions?
study.teachBack: What forms of protection does the stanza describe, and what does it not promise medically?

simple.en: The compassionate Divine gaze is praised as bringing comfort and abundance while keeping harm away.
simple.pa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ-ਦ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਨਾਲ ਸੁੱਖ, ਦਾਤ ਅਤੇ ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਾਅ ਦੀ ਅਸੀਸ ਦੱਸੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Grace and the language of blessings.
study.closeReading: The first two lines connect Divine regard with relief from burning distress; the last two name riddhi-siddhi and protection from a hostile shadow. Those terms live within religious poetry and require care in translation to avoid marketing supernatural or medical claims.

words.workingGloss: Abundance or auspicious prosperity; traditional term

study.interpretationCare: These lines cannot responsibly be presented as clinical cure claims, supernatural tests or promised financial results.
study.reflection: Can I be grateful for what I have without blaming those who are suffering?
study.teachBack: How do relief, gifts and shelter relate to the repeated idea of compassionate regard?

simple.en: Even a single heartfelt remembrance is praised in powerful language of freedom from fear, poverty and wrongdoing.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਕਾਲ ਦੇ ਡਰ, ਦਰਿਦ੍ਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੋਖ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ-ਤਸਵੀਰ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The remembered Name as spiritual refuge.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins with remembrance and the noose of death, then repeats the idea through speaking the Divine Name. Its final line gathers deprivation, hostility and moral failing into the need for deliverance. The unit is a prayer-poem, not a transactional formula.

words.workingGloss: Time, death or a Divine epithet, by context

study.interpretationCare: An interpretation that one recitation automatically clears debt or makes a person medically immortal is not supported as an empirical claim.
study.reflection: Where might sincere remembrance help me make steadier choices today?
study.teachBack: What does the repeated return to remembering the One contribute to the stanza?

simple.en: The prayer returns to surrender and support, concluding the SGPC-bounded Chaupai passage at the request to protect from harm.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ, ਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦੀ ਬੇਨਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਖਤਮ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ; SGPC-ਹੱਦ ਇੱਥੇ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An important edition and recitation boundary.
study.closeReading: Khargket is addressed as the protecting Divine; the speaker asks for rescue by hand and support everywhere. The last line, “dusht dokh te lehu bachai,” is the endpoint named in the SGPC Rehat Maryada’s specified Benti Chaupai selection. A reader should see this boundary before any extended source material.
study.interpretationCare: Our present 29-pauri candidate is broader than this SGPC excerpt. The next four pauris are tagged extended material, not silently included in every Nitnem convention.
study.reflection: How does preserving edition boundaries show respect for different Sikh practices?
study.teachBack: Which request ends this SGPC-bounded Chaupai selection?

simple.en: This extended-source stanza speaks of the grace of Jagmata and the completion of a granth.
simple.pa: ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਇਸ ਪਉੜੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਗਮਾਤਾ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਅਤੇ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Understanding the extended literary ending.
study.closeReading: The first half is explicitly authorial: gratitude to Jagmata and a statement that the granth was completed. The next half invokes cleansing of faults and defeat of wickedness. In our app this is extended source material beyond the SGPC-bounded Rehras excerpt, not a universal prayer obligation.

words.workingGloss: Mother of the world; traditional epithet in this text

study.interpretationCare: The authorship, narrative context, text boundaries and the meaning of Jagmata require competent independent Dasam source review.
study.reflection: How does noting the source boundary change the way I approach a familiar prayer?
study.teachBack: What evidence in the stanza suggests the poet is describing completion of a written work?

simple.en: The extended source praises the compassion of Asidhuj, links that grace with completing a granth, and speaks of blessings.
simple.pa: ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਵਾਲੇ ਭਾਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਸਿਧੁਜ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਭਲਾਈ ਦੀਆਂ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Blessings set within an authorial close.
study.closeReading: The initial words of the extended stanza continue the author’s account of the book’s completion. The following two lines speak in traditional devotional language of desired fruit and freedom from distress. This shift from writing a granth to blessing its listeners matters for explaining the text honestly.
study.interpretationCare: This is not a literal guarantee of every wish being granted or permanent freedom from injury, poverty or illness.
study.reflection: What would receiving a blessing mean without expecting a guaranteed outcome?
study.teachBack: How does the stanza connect completing the granth with the poet’s devotional hope?

simple.en: The extended verse uses strong traditional imagery of a speechless person gaining voice, an unknowing person gaining understanding, and fear being dispelled.
simple.pa: ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਗੂੰਗੇ ਨੂੰ ਬੋਲੀ, ਅਣਜਾਣ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਅਤੇ ਡਰ-ਦੁੱਖ ਤੋਂ ਛੁਟਕਾਰੇ ਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ-ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਵਰਤਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Reading religious blessing imagery responsibly.
study.closeReading: The first two lines depict seemingly miraculous change through attentive listening. The next two speak about relief from distress through recitation. The most respectful teaching records what the poem says, without confusing a statement of religious hope with an observable medical treatment effect or treating disability as moral inferiority.
study.interpretationCare: Never promise to cure speech disorders, disability, neurodevelopmental differences or medical illness by reciting or hearing Chaupai; appropriate clinical care remains important.
study.reflection: What can I learn from a text’s hope without using it to judge someone else’s disability?
study.teachBack: Which promises in this stanza must be distinguished from proven health outcomes?

simple.en: This extended concluding pauri records a traditional year, lunar date, weekday and location associated with the granth’s completion.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਅੰਤਲੇ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਮਤ, ਭਾਦੋਂ ਦੀ ਅੱਠਮੀ, ਐਤਵਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਲੁਜ ਕੰਢੇ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A colophon is historical source information, not a separate blessing.
study.closeReading: The four lines work together as a dating statement: the year is expressed in two parts, followed by bright-fortnight Ashtami in Bhadon and a Sunday, then a place near the Sutlej river. The wording serves as a textual colophon. Its calendar conversion, date consistency and provenance must be checked with a qualified editor.
study.interpretationCare: Do not convert the date silently to the Gregorian calendar, claim the edition universally authentic or present this colophon as a required paath for every Sikh.
study.reflection: Why is recording a source’s date and setting part of careful religious scholarship?
study.teachBack: Which four different kinds of dating or location information appear in these lines?

simple.en: The gift of Naam is received through the Divine and Guru’s grace, not won by anxious effort alone.
simple.pa: ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਦਾਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ; ਕੇਵਲ ਆਪਣੀ ਚਤੁਰਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Gift, wandering and acceptance of Hukam.
study.closeReading: The first two lines repeat that the gift is granted, then contrast wandering in bewilderment with lives being shaped through Naam. The fourth connects a clear mind with Guru’s grace and accepting bhana. The final line circles back to the opening, making grace the pauri’s recurring theme.

words.workingGloss: The Divine will; acceptance in this devotional context

study.interpretationCare: This is religious language about grace and agency, not a reason to deny individual responsibility or fail to seek practical assistance.
study.reflection: Where does striving help me, and where do I need humility about outcomes?
study.teachBack: What contrast does Pauri 8 draw between wandering and living in Naam?

simple.en: The pauri invites the sangat to approach the indescribable Divine through Guru, Hukam and true Bani.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਪਉੜੀ ਸੰਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ, ਹੁਕਮ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਚੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਅਕਥ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਨ ਦਾ ਸੱਦਾ ਦਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Community, surrender and the limits of speech.
study.closeReading: The repeated invitation to narrate the “akath” is deliberately paradoxical: the Divine exceeds description, yet the community is called to speak and sing. The centre names offering body, mind and possessions, following Hukam and the Guru’s Bani. It is not a request to surrender property to a person, but spiritual dedication in its scriptural setting.
study.interpretationCare: Do not use the language of offering wealth or obedience to justify exploitative authority, financial coercion or religious pressure; qualified Sikh review is required.
study.reflection: How can I participate in a shared practice without pretending I understand everything?
study.teachBack: Which practical steps follow the question about the “doorway” to the Unsayable?

simple.en: The mind’s ingenuity is not sufficient when Maya continually distracts it from remembrance.
simple.pa: ਮਾਇਆ ਦਾ ਮੋਹ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਭਟਕਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ; ਕੇਵਲ ਚਤੁਰਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸੂਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਦੀ।

study.focus: The ambivalence of Maya and cleverness.
study.closeReading: Opening and closing lines address the mind directly and repeat “chaturai.” Between them Maya is called enchanting and confusion-producing, yet also part of the Creator’s wondrous play. This is a more complex picture than declaring the material world simply bad: the issue is attachment that overtakes discernment.

words.workingGloss: Worldly appearance or the entangling attraction of things, context dependent

study.interpretationCare: Maya is a rich Sikh theological term; do not equate it simplistically with women, money, sensory experience or psychological illness.
study.reflection: Which kind of cleverness helps me learn, and when does it turn into evasion?
study.teachBack: Why does the stanza repeat “chaturai” before and after describing Maya?

simple.en: Love one’s family while remembering that worldly relationships and possessions cannot replace Truth.
simple.pa: ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰਦਿਆਂ ਵੀ ਸੱਚੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਆਸਰਾ ਬਣਾਉ।

study.focus: What accompanies the mind, and what does not.
study.closeReading: The first and last lines frame the pauri as counsel to the mind. Family is mentioned to illuminate impermanence, not to command abandonment. Between the questions about what accompanies us, the poem warns against acts of regret and points to the Guru’s teaching as enduring guidance.
study.interpretationCare: A spiritual verse about impermanence is never permission to neglect children, elders, spouse, safety or legitimate family responsibilities.
study.reflection: What would I do differently today if I remembered which actions I may later regret?
study.teachBack: What does the pauri distinguish between loving people and placing absolute dependence on transient ties?

simple.en: The Creator remains beyond complete description even while all living things appear within the Divine play.
simple.pa: ਸਾਰੀ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦਾ ਖੇਲ ਦਿੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਬੋਲ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਅੰਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੇ।

study.focus: Wonder without pretending total knowledge.
study.closeReading: The first two lines state the limitation of sense and knowledge; the third describes all life as the Creator’s play. The fourth turns toward Divine immanence: the One is present as speaker and witness in creation. The last repeats the unknowability, holding transcendence and immanence together.
study.interpretationCare: Neither these adjectives nor the cosmic “play” are empirical descriptions of a scientific mechanism. Respect the theological nuance of both presence and unknowability.
study.reflection: Can I remain curious without claiming certainty about everything?
study.teachBack: How does this pauri affirm both the One’s presence in creation and the limits of description?

simple.en: The amrit sought across the world is spoken of as the Guru’s gift, expressed through truth and release from ego.
simple.pa: ਦੁਨੀਆ ਜਿਸ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਦੀ ਭਾਲ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਬਾਣੀ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਆਤਮਕ ਦਾਤ ਦੱਸਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Search, grace and inner transformation.
study.closeReading: The opening lists diverse seekers, while the second line explains that the Guru brings the True One into the mind. The centre turns to creation, and the fourth offers a visible moral sign—greed and ego losing their hold. The final line completes the circle: amrit is received through grace, not purchased as a product.

words.workingGloss: Spiritual nectar, often linked to Naam in Gurbani

study.interpretationCare: Amrit here is devotional language and must not be misrepresented as a particular ingestible cure, secret supplement, or scientifically measurable substance.
study.reflection: Which desire or pride could I loosen as I reflect on this teaching?
study.teachBack: What change of behaviour accompanies the discovery of amrit in line four?

simple.en: The path of devotion demands humility and reduced greed, not spectacular displays or physical danger.
simple.pa: ਭਗਤੀ ਦੇ ਰਾਹ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ, ਲੋਭ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਰੀ ਤੇ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸਚਾਈ ਲੋੜੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਨਾ ਕਿ ਦਿਖਾਵਾ।

study.focus: Discipline framed by grace rather than performance.
study.closeReading: The first and last lines repeat that the path is different. The middle describes its difficult inner demands: leaving greed and self-centred habits, restraint in speech, and the imagery of razor-sharp narrowness. The fifth shows Guru’s grace rather than self-punishment as the source of change.

words.workingGloss: A sharpened blade or sword-edge, metaphorically

study.interpretationCare: Do not promote self-injury, dangerous challenges, extreme fasting or social withdrawal as required devotion. “Sharper than a blade” is not a literal activity.
study.reflection: How could I practise humility without turning it into another achievement?
study.teachBack: What practical habits accompany the blade-and-hair imagery?

simple.en: Guidance, grace and remembrance are connected in the poem’s vision of Hukam and the Guru’s teaching.
simple.pa: ਬਾਣੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਜ਼ਾ, ਕਿਰਪਾ, ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਮ-ਸਿਮਰਨ ਇੱਕ-ਦੂਜੇ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Hukam as orientation to remembrance.
study.closeReading: The pauri opens and closes by acknowledging the Divine direction of life. Between them it names the path, grace that brings Naam, and teaching heard through the Guru. Rather than resignation or passivity, the text describes an actively remembered relationship.

words.workingGloss: Through the Guru’s doorway or presence, context dependent

study.interpretationCare: “Gurdware” has both textual and institutional uses; do not silently impose one modern architectural reading on every historic occurrence.
study.reflection: What does it mean to walk responsibly within circumstances I cannot fully choose?
study.teachBack: Which of the middle lines connects guidance with active practice?

simple.en: The Guru’s Shabad is the enduring song of praise, experienced within rather than attained through talk alone.
simple.pa: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਹੀ ਅਸਲ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਹੈ; ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਬੋਲਣ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ, ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਉਣ ਨਾਲ ਅਰਥ ਬਣਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hearing, remembering and doing more than speaking.
study.closeReading: The repeated “shabad-sohila” frames the five lines; its inward dwelling is contrasted with aimless wandering and countless words. This is close to—but not the same source poem as—the separate five-shabad Kirtan Sohila night bani. The identity and musical meaning of “sohila” depend on context.

words.workingGloss: A song of joy or praise in this context

study.interpretationCare: Do not confuse this Anand Pauri with the separate Kirtan Sohila composition, nor claim that the same word guarantees identical musical settings.
study.reflection: Can my words about values become a habit I actually practise?
study.teachBack: What difference does the pauri describe between discussing the Shabad and letting it live in the mind?

simple.en: Remembrance transforms one’s own conduct and is celebrated as beneficial to family and sangat.
simple.pa: ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਦੇ ਜੀਵਨ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਵਾਰਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਤੇ ਸੰਗਤ ਤੱਕ ਭਲਾਈ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Purity as inward relationship and shared influence.
study.closeReading: The opening and closing lines define the theme through remembrance. The third line stretches this influence through parents, family and the full community, while the fourth connects speaking, hearing and inward holding of Naam. In this context purity is devotional and ethical language, not a social hierarchy.

words.workingGloss: Pure or spiritually cleansed, context dependent

study.interpretationCare: Do not tell someone that a relative’s illness, disability, social standing or bad luck reflects “impurity.” A poetic family blessing is not a medical guarantee.
study.reflection: What good habit could spread quietly through my household or community?
study.teachBack: Which verbs describe what a person does with the Bani: speaking, listening and what else?
